findings.text: Periodic tick service clears the forced event marker and runs per CPU periodic accounting, then returns early when the device handler has moved away from periodic mode or the device is not in oneshot state, otherwise it repeatedly advances the deadline by one tick and reprograms the event device until programming succeeds.

Broadcast oneshot control consults the current CPU tick device and does nothing for devices lacking stop in idle capability, otherwise it forwards the requested broadcast state to the internal control helper whose fallback variant reports a busy failure.
Timekeeping handover assertion warns when executed on the CPU currently designated as the do timer timekeeper, indicating the caller incorrectly retained timekeeping duty across handover.

CPU teardown transfers do timer ownership from the dying CPU to the first online CPU, marks scheduler tick state so the outgoing CPU cannot retake duty, cancels any high resolution scheduler timer, clears the per CPU scheduler tick structure while preserving idle accounting counters, and detaches the CPU from timer broadcast handling. A header variant provides a no operation teardown when scheduler tick support is absent.

Local suspend shuts down the current CPU clock event device, global suspend additionally suspends broadcast distribution, and header fallbacks reduce broadcast suspend and global suspend to no operations when the corresponding support is not compiled.

Freeze and unfreeze form a depth counted barrier across online CPUs where each arrival increments depth under protection, the final arrival transitions system state and suspends scheduler clock and timekeeping while the first arrival on resume restores timekeeping and scheduler clock and returns the system to running, and non final participants only suspend or resume their local tick device.

Freeze barrier serialization uses a raw spinlock guarding the depth counter, with an additional lock dependency map acquisition around the uncontended transition section to document absence of concurrency while other CPUs wait with interrupts disabled.

Timekeeping suspend samples the persistent clock, notes persistent clock existence when the sample is nonzero, forwards the shadow timekeeper to current time, flags the system as suspended, captures the active monotonic clock and cycle counter for suspend timing, applies drift compensation against the previous suspend delta, publishes shadow state, freezes fast readers, then suspends tick, clocksource and clock event layers.

Timekeeping resume samples the persistent clock, resumes clock events and clocksources, then under protection prefers elapsed time from nonstop suspend timing and falls back to persistent clock advance, injects any found sleep interval, rebases monotonic and raw cycle markers to the current cycle, clears NTP error and the suspended flag, publishes shadow state with a clock was set notification, and finally resumes tick handling and notifies timer file descriptors.

Sleep injection validates the delta strictly and aborts with a deferred warning on invalid input, otherwise it advances wall time, shifts wall to monotonic offset backward by the same delta, accumulates boot offset and its timespec mirror with ordered writes, and records the interval in sleep time debug bins where enabled.

Suspend drift handling keeps a static previous delta between system time and persistent time, replaces it when the change reaches two seconds on the assumption of an external correction, otherwise folds the change back into the recorded suspend timestamp to keep long term offset stable, and unconditionally requests suspend timing.

Suspend halts fast time readers by copying current monotonic and raw bases into a static dummy holder, sampling the suspend cycle count, redirecting both fast bases to a dummy clock while preserving real base plus offset for monotonic, and publishing the frozen copies.
A weak default persistent clock reader reports zero seconds and nanoseconds, allowing platforms without a persistent clock to link while platform code may override it.

Early tick initialization establishes broadcast and no hertz support, while full dynticks initialization exits when full mode is disabled, requires architecture support for self triggered IRQ work, removes the boot CPU from the full mask under sleep on nonzero restrictions, enables user tracking on each full CPU, and registers a hotplug predown hook and reports the resulting mask.
Timer event tracking pairs two unsigned sixty four bit counters named local and global inside a small aggregate used to compare per CPU and system wide timer deadlines.
Sentinel CPU identifiers mark absence of a do timer owner with negative one and boot time ownership with negative two.
The jiffies shift scaling factor takes the value six, seven or eight depending on configuration variant.
Wall clock notification mask groups realtime, realtime soft, TAI and TAI soft high resolution timer bases, while boot clock mask groups boottime and boottime soft bases.
Stalled jiffies tolerance is five ticks before a non owner attempts a limited jiffies update.

Legacy tick path conditionally advances jiffies under jiffies lock and sequence protection when ticks elapsed, refreshes wall time, then runs process time accounting in the interrupted context mode and invokes CPU profiling.

Jiffies writers serialize with a raw jiffies spinlock plus a sequence counter begun before and ended after jiffies and period mutation, while timekeeper state uses an interrupt saving raw spinlock across forward, suspend and resume mutations, and boot offset uses ordered write access paired with readers.

Sixty four bit builds use a lock free acquire check of the next tick deadline and skip work when now precedes it, thirty two bit builds sample the deadline under sequence retry, both recheck under lock to filter duplicate updates, then advance jiffies by one plus any whole missed periods, refresh the last update stamp and next deadline with release ordering on sixty four bit, close the sequence, compute global load under lock, release the lock and refresh wall time.

Scheduler timer duty adopts ownership when the recorded owner indicates none by writing the current CPU, updates jiffies only on the owner, tracks consecutive ticks without jiffies movement per scheduler state, resets on progress, and after the stall threshold attempts a single winner atomic gated limited update that only proceeds when this scheduler instance last observed the same jiffies value.

No hertz timer callback runs timer duty and, when interrupt registers are present, runs scheduler handling otherwise clearing the next tick marker, returns without restart while the stopped flag is set to defer reprogramming to idle or IRQ exit, otherwise forwards the high resolution timer by one tick period and requests restart. Scheduler handling refreshes soft lockup supervision and clears next tick when stopped before running process accounting and profiling.
Per CPU scheduler tick state lives in a per CPU instance and is retrieved for any CPU through an accessor returning a pointer to that CPU slot, with flag clearing requiring interrupts disabled.

Timer migration hierarchy walk starts from a child group and climbs parents via ordered reads that synchronize with group linkage publication, propagating each visited group mask as the child mask for the next iteration, invoking a caller callback that can stop the walk. Remote handling requirement reports false in this configuration.

Warn once hazards cover hierarchy level exceeding configured depth, empty child mask during upward walk, timekeeping handover invoked on the timekeeper CPU itself, and full dynticks enabled without architecture self interrupt support or with illegal boot CPU membership or with unexpected duty loss.

Periodic oneshot emulation must be backed by a genuine hardware time source before repeatedly running periodic accounting while reprogramming fails, otherwise accounting driven time advance can cause repeated reprogramming attempts.

Several header helpers collapse to empty operations when support is disabled, including periodic broadcast, oneshot broadcast check on this CPU, broadcast initialization, no hertz initialization, scheduler clock suspend and resume, broadcast suspend, global tick suspend, scheduler timer teardown, and sleep time debug accounting.
